stories.title: At least 9 killed in hotel fire in India’s Kolkata
stories.summary: A fire in a Kolkata hotel killed nine people, including a child, possibly caused by a faulty air conditioner, with thick smoke trapping guests inside. Sixty guests were staying in the hotel; six were injured and taken to hospital, with some victims likely Bangladeshi nationals visiting for medical treatment. Authorities are investigating safety lapses, while firefighters faced challenges due to dense smoke; Prime Minister Modi expressed condolences and support for the victims. A fire ripped through a hotel in the Indian city of Kolkata on Aug 19, killing nine people, authorities said, with investigators suspecting a faulty air conditioner may be the cause. “Nine people were killed, including a child, in the fire that broke out early on Wednesday,” Anuj Sharma, the fire services director of West Bengal state, told AFP. “Thick smoke enveloped the hotel. Some victims were found in the bathrooms.” Building fires are common in India due to a lack of firefighting equipment and routine disregard for safety regulations. Preliminary information suggested an air conditioner in the budget hotel may have exploded and caused the blaze, Sharma said. A forensic team was deployed to examine the scene after the fire had been brought under control. Sixty guests were staying at the hotel, police said in a statement. Media reports said six people were injured and taken to hospital for treatment.
